text:
Maria: Heads-up — a customer running Redwood Private in their VPC asked for the ability to upload and enforce their own rate-limit policies (per-org + per-key + burst windows) without routing all checks through our control plane.
Kevin: Clarify: do they want the policy to be authoritative locally (i.e., enforcement happens inside their VPC) or just a UI to manage limits that we still enforce server-side?
Maria: Authoritative locally. They want to manage spike protection and burst tokens themselves for compliance reasons. Billing still goes through Redwood, but enforcement should be possible without control-plane roundtrips for every request.
Sam: Implementation thoughts: we can do this two ways — lightweight in-VPC rate-limiter at the edge (envoy filter / sidecar) or an OPA-style policy engine that evaluates policies and returns allow/deny + quota tokens. Edge approach is lower latency.
Sam: Example policy idea (YAML):
```yaml
policy_version: v1
scope: org
rules:
  - subject: api_key
    limit: 1000
    window_sec: 60
    burst: 200
    actions:
      - throttle: true
```
Sam: The edge component would maintain counters locally with a configurable sync/telemetry channel for aggregated usage.
Anya: Telemetry question — how do we keep billing accurate if enforcement is local? They may not want itemized usage sent to Redwood.
Maria: Two options for billing: 1) mandatory aggregated metering agent that sends signed, batched counters; 2) require customers to attach signed attestations and run a monthly audit (less ideal). We should let customers opt into the metering agent; for enterprises, contract terms can require it.
Julien: Security note — if enforcement is entirely customer-controlled we need to avoid spoofing/misreporting. Recommend mutual TLS between metering agent and our intake, and signed policy manifests. Also periodic attestation checks from our side to verify agent integrity.
Kevin: UX suggestion for Console: show "Local rate policy" tab under Private deployments with a diff view, validation, and a "simulate" button that runs sample load and previews dropped requests. Validation should catch incompatible fields (e.g., negative burst, unsupported window sizes).
Kevin: Policy JSON sketch for console preview:
```json
{
  "subject": "api_key",
  "limit": 1000,
  "window_sec": 60,
  "burst": 200
}
```

Sam: A few engineering constraints:
- We need deterministic eviction for counters to avoid unbounded memory.
- Support for multiple clock skews across nodes (use lease/owner for windows).
- Graceful fallback: if local policy subsystem crashes, we should fall back to a configured remote policy or allow configurable default.
Anya: Ops ask — we should expose per-route telemetry (token counts, dropped) as aggregated metrics to Prometheus/Datadog. Customer-managed deployments might push metrics to a s3-compatible endpoint and optionally to our intake with PII scrubbed.
Julien: Also decide on policy format (we should standardize on a small subset of fields initially). Avoid full Turing-complete policy language for now.
Maria: Action items: Sam to draft design doc covering edge component, policy format, telemetry contract, and threat model. Kevin to draft console wireframe for policy upload/preview. Julien to list security requirements for signed manifests and MTLS. Due: 2 weeks. Owner: Sam.
ops-bot: Created INF-5123 (Private rate-limits: delegated enforcement) and linked to this thread :white_check_mark:
Maria: Thanks — I'll sync with the account team and push the customer ask into the RFC.
